City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 17, 2023  2

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – SEPTEMBER 2023

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2023-2024 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 23-36) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2023-24 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for September 2023.

  D. FISCAL YEAR 2022-23 YEAR-END APPROPRIATION ADJUSTMENTS

  As the City’s Fiscal Year 2022-23 financial books are being closed, it becomes
  necessary to make budget adjustments prior to the forthcoming audit. These
  adjustments are necessary to allocate additional funds to general fund
  departments or other funds that have surpassed their initially-allocated or
  amended budgets. These budget adjustments may involve transferring
  appropriations between general fund departments or appropriating funds to
  a fund that has exceeded is budgeted appropriations. General fund
  departments and funds that exceed approved budgets are disclosed in
  audited financial statements.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-66
  approving proposed amendments to the annual budget for Fiscal Year 2022-
  23.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 17, 2023  3
   E. APPROVAL OF  FINAL PARCEL MAP NO. 74404, A 2-UNIT
  CONDOMINIUM  DEVELOPMENT PROJECT LOCATED AT 321 W.
  GLENDON WAY

  The development project located at 321 West Glendon Way is a 2-unit
  condominium on a 9,734-square-foot lot. Staff and RKA Consulting Group
  Incorporated (RKA), the City’s contract consultant for land surveying, have
  reviewed the Final Parcel Map and determined that it is in compliance with
  the State Subdivision Map Act, Conditions of Approval, and the City’s
  ordinances regarding subdivision. There is no fiscal impact related to this
  item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The project has
  been reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), and is exempt from CEQA based on Section 15332, Class 32 exemption
  (In-Fill Development).

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Final Parcel Map No. 74404,
  authorize its filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder and authorize the
  City Manager to execute the Subdivision Agreement on behalf of the City.

  F. RESOLUTION NO. 23-64 APPROVING A REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURE ON THE 800 BLOCK OF COMMERCIAL AVENUE

  The Public Works Department received a request from Jason De La Torre,
  owner of the property located at 864 Commercial Avenue, for a temporary
  street closure. The purpose of this request is to hold a private event on
  Saturday, November 11, 2023, on the 800 block of Commercial Avenue from
  2:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. Ogopogo has had multiple prior street closure events;
  the City has not experienced any significant adverse issues from those prior
  events. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-64
  authorizing closure on the 800 block of Commercial Avenue from South
  Gladys Avenue to the end of the cul-de-sac from 2:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. on
  Saturday November 11, 2023.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 17, 2023  4
   G. POLICE DEPARTMENT PURCHASE OF NEW POLICE MOTORCYCLE IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $39,125.47

  One of the frontline police motorcycles has over 135,000 miles of use. It is
  being operated far beyond the normal service life and is exhibiting significant
  mechanical issues. The Police Department has budgeted to replace a 2018
  BMW motorcycle in this Fiscal Year (FY) 2023-2024. The Police Department
  has budgeted approximately $40,000 for the purchase of a new Police
  Motorcycle. The quote provided by Long Beach BMW Motorcycle reflects the
  best possible price for a fully-outfitted 2024 BMW RT1250. The current quote
  reflects the total price including tax as well as the motorcycle helmet and
  radio installation for a price of $39,125.47.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Chief of Police to utilize
  “piggyback” pricing from Los Angeles County Sheriff’s contract #PO-SH-
  23008318-1 for the purchase of one 2024 BMW RT1250 at a cost of
  $39,125.47 from Long Beach BMW Motorcycles utilizing capital outlay funds
  from account #124-751-37-99-201.

  H. OFFICER WELLNESS AND MENTAL HEALTH GRANT ACCEPTANCE AND
  EXPENDITURE

  The City of San Gabriel, Police Department, has been awarded grant funds by
  the Board of State and Community Corrections (BSCC) in the amount of
  $32,997.89 to improve officer wellness and mental health throughout the
  organization. The funds provided from the Wellness and Mental Health grant
  will pay for memberships at health and fitness clubs. There will be no impact
  on the regular budget of the Police Department.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to accept
  the BSCC Award of $32,997.89; and adopt Resolution No. 23-58 amending the
  Fiscal Year 2022-23, Other Grants Fund 186. The expenditure account to

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 17, 2023  5
   appropriate the budget is #124-751-57-96-174 for the Officer Wellness and
  Mental Health Grant Program.

  I. 2020 STATE HOMELAND SECURITY PROGRAM – PART 2 GRANT
  ACCEPTANCE AND EXPENDITURE AUTHORIZATION IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $14,447

  The City of San Gabriel has been awarded and accepted grant funds from the
  2020 State Homeland Security Program (SHSP) for Fire Departments in the
  amount of $62,000. The Fire Departments has been able to use these funds
  towards projects from the Department of Homeland Security Approved
  Equipment List. An additional amount of $14,447 was granted this year, which
  could be used to complete purchasing and issuance of protective equipment
  for Fire Department personnel.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-65
  authorizing the following:

  1. Increase estimated revenue (account 186-3215) and appropriation
  (transfers out) in “other Grants” Fund by $14,447; and increase estimated
  revenue (transfers in) and appropriation in Capital/Special Projects Funds
  (account #124-761-57-99-380) by $14,447.
  2. Authorize the Fire Chief to use the additional SHSP grant money, in the
  amount of $14,447 to purchase qualifying equipment under the City’s
  purchasing policy.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. PICKLEBALL DISCUSSION - OPTIONS FOR THE ADDITION OF PICKLEBALL
  COURTS IN SAN GABRIEL

  During the July 18, 2023 City Council Meeting, staff presented a construction
  contract for a new pickleball court at Smith Park. At that meeting, public
  comments and a petition were presented speaking against the construction of

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 17, 2023  6
   the new court. After much deliberation, the City Council requested to have the
  item come back at a future meeting. The item was presented again at the
  August 15, 2023 meeting and again there were many public comments about
  the item. Council requested that the item come back with potential options at
  a future meeting. Should the Council choose Alternative 1, the cost of
  resurfacing and painting of the courts has already been approved by the City
  Council. If, after further evaluation, there is a need for expansion of the court
  (i.e. extending the court) to accommodate four pickleball courts, staff will
  bring that forward to the City Council for approval of the enhancements to
  the court. Should the City Council choose Option 2 or 3 for the construction
  of a pickleball court at another location, staff would bring an item forward to
  include construction/resurfacing costs for the approved location.

  ALTERNATIVES

  Alternative 1: Continue with the courts as existing. When resurfacing the
  courts, as already approved by Council, resurface one for tennis play only and
  one with four permanent pickleball courts for pickleball play only. Staff will
  evaluate the court spacing to place four pickleball courts on the tennis court
  and, if needed, will bring an item back to the Council for expansion of the
  court. Sound barriers would also be placed on the courts at Smith. Should the
  pool expansion move forward, staff recommends evaluating the site to
  potentially add a pickleball court to the east of the current courts and moving
  the pool further east.

  Alternative 2: Convert both of the existing courts at Smith Park to permanent
  pickleball courts (eight courts). Staff will evaluate the court spacing to place
  eight pickleball courts on the courts and, if needed, will bring an item back to
  the Council for expansion of the courts. Sound barriers would also be placed
  on the courts at Smith. Should the pool expansion move forward, staff
  recommends evaluating the site to potentially add a tennis court or additional
  pickleball court to the east of the current courts and moving the pool further
  east.

  Alternative 3: Locate permanent pickleball courts next to the existing
  basketball courts in Smith Park.

  Alternative 4: Locate two permanent pickleball courts in Lugo Park with
  possible options.

  Alternative 5: This option would be to continue with the courts as existing, not
  adding additional courts. Current courts at Smith Park and Washington School

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 17, 2023  7
   Park would be resurfaced as previously approved by the City Council, but no
  courts would be added.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Depending on the
  alternative selected by the Council, project is exempt under following
  exemptions: Class 1 (e)(2)(A)(B) Existing Facilities, Class 3 New Construction of
  Small Structures or Class 11 Accessory Structures.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council proceed with Alternative 1.

  B. IMPACT FEE CALCULATION REVISION,  ORDINANCE  NO.  697  –
  INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  In 2004, the City Council adopted Chapter 154 of the San Gabriel Municipal
  Code to establish Development Impact Fees for new development. In 2015,
  the City adopted Resolution No. 24-38, which increased the Open Space and
  Recreation Development Impact Fees and how the impact fee calculations are
  applicable to residential additions. The City adopted new regulations for
  Accessory Dwelling Units (ADU) in 2020. The City estimates a revenue
  reduction of $30,000 from non-ADU residential projects and a revenue
  increase of $180,000 from ADU projects based upon Fiscal Year 2022/2023
  issued permits. These fees are recorded in the development impact fee fund,
  and there is no impact to the general fund.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that that City Council waive full reading and introduce by
  title only Ordinance No. 697: An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of
  San Gabriel, California, Amending Title XV Chapter 154 (Development Impact
  Fees) in Order to Amend the Impact Fees Proration Rate Calculation Formula,
  which would revise the current impact fee calculation methodology for non-
  ADU additions and new single-family dwellings and ADUs over 750 square
  feet to be as follows:

  Non-ADU additions and New Single-Family Dwellings:
  (Added square feet)/1,000 multiplied by the residential impact fees up to
  100% or 50% if an existing dwelling is removed. No exemption for projects
  under 25% of the original dwelling size.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 17, 2023  8
   ADUs over 750 square feet:
  (Square feet above 750 square feet)/250 multiplied by the residential impact
  fees up to the limit imposed by state law. Note that ADUs in San Gabriel have
  a maximum size of 1,000 square feet and all new primary dwelling impact fees
  are the same regardless of size. Establish a new primary dwelling base size of
  1,000 square feet for calculation reference of full single family unit impact
  fees.

  The second reading and adoption will be scheduled at the next regular
  Council Meeting.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT
  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
